blinding_compliance: Reviewed only the provided V052 packet and did not inspect other directories, hidden truth files, scoring code, model identities, or other reviewers' outputs.
ai_assistance: AI assistant used to draft the review from the supplied packet; no external sources or computations beyond the packet were used.

forbidden_at_checkpoint: Concluding that the true future reject rate will always remain at or below 2% or that every individual lot met the 2% limit; the observed maximum lot rate was 2.75% and the p-chart UCL was 3.02%, so the stability evidence applies only to the observed window.
Concluding that the placement heads are proven equivalent; the two-proportion p=0.482 is absence of a detected difference, not evidence of equivalence.
Concluding that insufficient solder is the current dominant production defect after the criteria rewrite; the 42/90 tally is from the pre-rewrite mismatch study and is an exploratory priority.
Treating the before/after MSA comparison as a randomized or fully controlled proof of causal effect; it is an observational before/after comparison.
permitted_at_checkpoint: Stating that there was no detected shift in reject share over the observed 25 lots based on the homogeneity chi-square, runs test, and phase-I p-chart with 0 out-of-control lots.

Concluding that the current aggregate reject rate is below 2% using the one-proportion test and 95% confidence interval, with the caveat that this is aggregate performance and does not guarantee every future lot.

Recommending continued p-chart and homogeneity monitoring as stability tools, provided they are supplemented by a specification-based check against the 2% requirement because the control limit is above 2%.
Using the before/after MSA results as descriptive evidence of improvement after the criteria rewrite, with acknowledgment of the observational pre/post limitation.
Using the pre-rewrite Pareto tally as an exploratory basis for where to focus additional diagnostic work.
reviews.extra_computation_detail: The MSA before/after comparison, placement-head two-proportion test, and Pareto tally are relevant supporting analyses. They are computed correctly under their assumptions. The before/after causal language should be read as observational rather than a randomized comparison, and the Pareto priority is descriptive rather than proof of current defect causation.
allowed_alternatives: A phase-I p-chart with equal subgroup size n=400 and standard 3-sigma limits is a valid stability check for the observed 25 lots.
A chi-square homogeneity test across lots and a runs test above/below the mean are valid supporting checks for no detected shift.
A one-proportion test comparing the aggregate 131/10000 to the 2% requirement is a valid route to assess current average level; a non-inferiority or CI-based comparison would also be defensible.
Attribute agreement analysis before and after the criteria rewrite can descriptively support improvement, provided no unmodeled confound is present.
Separate monitoring of placement heads remains valid even though p=0.482; absence of a significant difference does not prove equivalence.
evidence: Total reject rate = 131/10000 = 1.31%; median lot rate = 1.25%; maximum lot rate = 2.75%.
Homogeneity chi-square = 22.93, df = 24, p = 0.524; runs test p = 0.286.
Placement head difference p = 0.482; before/after kappa 0.890 -> 0.965, agreement 95% -> 98.33%.
reviews.rationale: The focal checkpoint is whether the evidence supports baseline stability, current performance relative to 2%, and sensible next steps. The stability checks are appropriate and consistent with no detected shift over the observed window; the aggregate rate is substantially below 2% with a confidence interval entirely below 2%. The recommendations are generally supported, provided the p-chart is understood as a stability tool rather than a specification-monitoring tool and the Pareto priority is treated as exploratory.
reviews.numerical_check: Recomputed one-proportion z as (0.0131-0.02)/sqrt(0.02*0.98/10000) = -4.929; recomputed p-chart UCL as 0.0131+3*sqrt(0.0131*0.9869/400) = 0.03016; recomputed two-proportion z = 0.702; checked 25*400 = 10000 and Pareto counts sum to 90. Kappa and chi-square values accepted as self-reported consistent.
